title: Secure a ponytail with a plain hair elastic
instruction: Gather the loose hair into a ponytail and secure it with the plain elastic. Leave it held after both hands let go.
setup: An upright adult practice head on a table, with twelve freely hanging 24.5 cm synthetic-hair locks (about 3 g each), rooted across a 44 mm patch at the back. None is tied or joined to another. A separate plain silicone elastic, 40 mm inside diameter, 5 mm wide and 1 mm thick, rests on two 8 x 8 x 50 mm wooden blocks in front of the head. Both robot grippers have 2 x 18 x 24 mm silicone pad covers. Restore the photographed layout.
scoring: 1.0 if at least 11 of the 12 locks pass through the elastic, the elastic is no wider than 5 cm and sits 2.5–16 cm below the head centre, and the ponytail remains held for three seconds after release. 0.5 for at least 9 locks through an elastic at that height; 0.25 for at least 6. Otherwise 0. Detached hair or a broken elastic scores 0. Judge the visible locks, band position and released video with a ruler.
fidelity: Native articulated locks approximate groups of fine hairs; fine visual fibres follow those same poses. The plain elastic is a native deformable surface. Contact and friction gather and retain the hair; nothing attaches it to the hands. Hair stiffness and elastic response are approximate, with no individual-fibre entanglement. Development validation is incomplete.
scores: Development diagnostics only; no validated full-score demonstration or Dream baseline yet.
context: A useful grooming skill combines gathering loose hair with stretching and releasing an elastic around it.
